13375-the-rival-heirs-being-the-third-an.creator: Rev. A. D. Crake.
13375-the-rival-heirs-being-the-third-an.description: A book by Rev. A. D. Crake.. The writer was for many years the chaplain of a large school, and it was his desire to make the leisure hours of Sunday bright and happy, in the absence of the sports and pastimes of weekdays.

33615-three-young-ranchmen-or-daring-adv.creator: The Saalfield Publishing Company
33615-three-young-ranchmen-or-daring-adv.description: A book by The Saalfield Publishing Company. "We will have to content ourselves on the ranch another year, I am afraid. Father left matters in a very unsettled condition, and what has become of Uncle Barnaby the world only knows."

3787-nature-and-art.title: Nature And Art
3787-nature-and-art.creator: Mrs. Inchbald.
3787-nature-and-art.description: A book by Mrs. Inchbald.. impediment in speech made it impossible for Mrs. Inchbald to succeed greatly as an actress. She was unable to realise her own conceptions. At times she and her husband prospered so little that on one day their dinner was of turnips, pulled and eaten in a field, and sometimes there was no dinner at all.

arxiv-2205-01447.title: Model-Free Opponent Shaping
arxiv-2205-01447.creator: Chris Lu, Timon Willi, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Jakob Foerster
arxiv-2205-01447.description: Abstract In general-sum games, the interaction of self-interested learning agents commonly leads to collectively worst-case outcomes, such as defect-defect in the iterated prisoner’s dilemma (IPD). To overcome this, some methods, such as Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), shape their opponents’ learning process.

arxiv-2207-10591.title: FDD Massive MIMO Channel Training: Optimal Rate-Distortion Bounds and the Efficiency of “one-shot” Schemes
arxiv-2207-10591.creator: Mahdi Barzegar Khalilsarai, Yi Song, Tianyu Yang, Giuseppe Caire
arxiv-2207-10591.description: Abstract We study the problem of providing channel state information (CSI) at the transmitter in multi-user “massive” MIMO systems operating in frequency division duplexing (FDD). The wideband MIMO channel is a vector-valued random process correlated in time, space (antennas), and frequency (subcarriers).

arxiv-2409-04819.title: Top-GAP: Integrating Size Priors in CNNs for more Interpretability, Robustness, and Bias Mitigation
arxiv-2409-04819.creator: Lars Nieradzik, Henrike Stephani, Janis Keuper
arxiv-2409-04819.description: Abstract This paper introduces Top-GAP, a novel regularization technique that enhances the explainability and robustness of convolutional neural networks. By constraining the spatial size of the learned feature representation, our method forces the network to focus on the most salient image regions, effectively reducing background influence.

arxiv-2409-12272.title: Mastering Chess with a Transformer Model
arxiv-2409-12272.creator: Daniel Monroe, Philip A. Chalmers
arxiv-2409-12272.description: Abstract Transformer models have demonstrated impressive capabilities when trained at scale, excelling at difficult cognitive tasks requiring complex reasoning and rational decision-making. In this paper, we explore the application of transformers to chess, focusing on the critical role of the position representation within the attention mechanism.

arxiv-2411-04113.title: Ultralow loss torsion micropendula for chipscale gravimetry
arxiv-2411-04113.creator: C. A. Condos, J. R. Pratt, J. Manley, A. R. Agrawal, S. Schlamminger, C. M. Pluchar, D. J. Wilson
arxiv-2411-04113.description: Abstract We explore a new class of chipscale torsion pendula formed by Si 3 N 4 nanoribbon suspensions. Owing to their unique hierarchy of gravitational, tensile, and elastic stiffness, the devices exhibit damping rates of ∼ 10 ​ μ \sim 10\;\mu Hz and parametric gravity sensitivities near that of an ideal pendulum.

arxiv-2411-07585.title: Reinforcement Learning Framework for Quantitative Trading
arxiv-2411-07585.creator: Alhassan S. Yasin, Prabdeep S. Gill
arxiv-2411-07585.description: Abstract . The inherent volatility and dynamic fluctuations within the financial stock market underscore the necessity for investors to employ a comprehensive and reliable approach that integrates risk management strategies, market trends, and the movement trends of individual securities. By evaluating specific data, investors can make more informed decisions.

arxiv-2502-07067.title: Repository-level Code Search with Neural Retrieval Methods
arxiv-2502-07067.creator: Siddharth Gandhi, Luyu Gao, Jamie Callan
arxiv-2502-07067.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Siddharth Gandhi, Luyu Gao, Jamie Callan. This paper presents a multi-stage reranking system for repository-level code search, which leverages the vastly available commit histories of large open-source repositories to aid in bug fixing. We define the task of repository-level code search as retrieving the set of files from the current state of a code repository that are most relevant to addressing a user’s question or bug.

arxiv-2503-06999.title: Encoding Schemes for Parallel In-Place Algorithms
arxiv-2503-06999.creator: Chase Hutton, Adam Melrod
arxiv-2503-06999.description: Abstract . Many parallel algorithms which solve basic problems in computer science use auxiliary space linear in the input to facilitate conflict-free computation. There has been significant work on improving these parallel algorithms to be in-place, that is to use as little auxiliary memory as possible.

arxiv-2504-16849.title: Magnetorotational instability in a solar near-surface mean-field dynamo
arxiv-2504-16849.creator: Axel Brandenburg, Gustav Larsson, Fabio Del Sordo, Petri J. Käpylä
arxiv-2504-16849.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Axel Brandenburg, Gustav Larsson, Fabio Del Sordo, Petri J. Käpylä. We address the question whether the magnetorotational instability (MRI) can operate in the near-surface shear layer (NSSL) of the Sun and how it affects the interaction with the dynamo process. Using hydromagnetic mean-field simulations of α ​ Ω \alpha\Omega -type dynamos in rotating shearing-periodic boxes, we show that for negative shear, the MRI can operate above a certain critical shear parameter.

arxiv-2506-16234.title: Think Global, Act Local: Bayesian Causal Discovery with Language Models in Sequential Data
arxiv-2506-16234.creator: Prakhar Verma, David Arbour, Sunav Choudhary, Harshita Chopra, Arno Solin, Atanu R. Sinha
arxiv-2506-16234.description: Abstract Causal discovery from observational data typically assumes full access to data and availability of domain experts. In practice, data often arrive in batches, and expert knowledge is scarce. Language Models (LMs) offer a surrogate but come with their own issues—hallucinations, inconsistencies, and bias.

arxiv-2507-05842.title: Bounded diameter monochromatic component covers
arxiv-2507-05842.creator: Alexey Pokrovskiy
arxiv-2507-05842.description: Abstract Ryser conjectured that every r r -edge-coloured complete graph can be covered by r − 1 r-1 monochromatic trees. Motivated by a question of Austin in analysis, Milićević predicted something stronger — that every r r -edge-coloured complete graph can be covered by r − 1 r-1 monochromatic trees of bounded diameter .

arxiv-2510-11946.title: Universality of the chiral soliton lattice in the low energy limit of QCD
arxiv-2510-11946.creator: Fabrizio Canfora, Nicolás Grandi, Marcela Lagos, Luis Urrutia-Reyes, Aldo Vera
arxiv-2510-11946.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Fabrizio Canfora, Nicolás Grandi, Marcela Lagos, Luis Urrutia-Reyes, Aldo Vera. In this paper, we show that the chiral soliton lattice (ChSL) is, in a precise sense, a universal feature of the low-energy limit of QCD minimally coupled to Maxwell theory.

pmc-11393300.title: Faculty consensus on competitiveness for the new competency‐based emergency medicine standardized letter of evaluation
pmc-11393300.creator: Benjamin Schnapp, Morgan Sehdev, Caitlin Schrepel, Sharon Bord, Alexis Pelletier‐Bui, Alai Alvarez, Nicole M Dubosh, Yoon Soo Park, Eric Shappell
pmc-11393300.description: BackgroundEmergency medicine (EM) has introduced a new, competency‐based standardized letter of evaluation (SLOE) template. While a previous version of the SLOE has been shown to promote a high degree of faculty consensus regarding competitiveness, this has not been shown for the new SLOE template.ObjectiveThe objective was to evaluate faculty consensus on competitiveness for the new EM SLOE 2.0.

pmc-11572361.title: Comparative transcriptomic and hormonal analyses reveal potential regulation networks of adventitious root formation in Metasequoia glyptostroboides Hu et Cheng
pmc-11572361.creator: Yuping Xiong, Xiaohong Chen, Junyu Liu, Yuan Li, Zhan Bian, Xinhua Zhang, Songjun Zeng, Jaime A Teixeira da Silva, Guohua Ma
pmc-11572361.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe extract from Metasequoia glyptostroboides Hu et Cheng, a rare and endangered species native to China, exhibits numerous biological and pharmacological activities. The species is recalcitrant to rooting during micropropagation, a challenge that has yet to be resolved. In this study, transcriptomic and hormonal analyses were conducted to appreciate the molecular mechanism of adventitious root (AR) formation in optimized rooting conditions.ResultsThe use of 2/5-strength Woody Plant Medium (WPM) significantly promoted AR formation of M.

pmc-11624671.title: Atrial Fibrillation Types and Chronic Kidney Disease are Independent Predictors of Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Radiofrequency Ablation
pmc-11624671.creator: Pei Mo, Cheng Fan, Jiayuan Chen, Yu Wang, Wenhao Xiao, Zhiguo Peng, Xiao-Zhen Lin, Cheng-Feng Luo, Chongyu Zhang
pmc-11624671.description: PurposeAtrial fibrillation (AF) is classified into paroxysmal, persistent, long-term persistent, and permanent types. It is commonly treated by radiofrequency ablation (RFA), which is more successful than conventional anti-arrhythmic drugs, but it is still largely unknown whether these beneficial effects are equally present for all AF types.

pmc-12500987.title: The role of dorsomedial striatum and parvalbumin interneurons in schizophrenia-related cognitive deficits: insights from disrupted strategic decision-making in Akt1 heterozygous mice
pmc-12500987.creator: Chia-Yuan Chang, Ching Chen, Ya-Wen Liu, Shiang-Shin Gau, Yu-Ling Pan, Wen-Sung Lai
pmc-12500987.description: Schizophrenia, a debilitating disorder with genetic and neurobiological underpinnings, often manifests cognitive deficits, including impaired decision-making. Utilizing Akt1 heterozygous mutant (HET) mice as a model, which mimic schizophrenia due to AKT1’s implication as a susceptibility gene, we investigated the involvement of Akt1 and its neural mechanisms influencing strategic decision-making to identify potential therapeutic targets for schizophrenia-associated cognitive impairments.

pmc-13026552.title: Effects of Task-Oriented Circuit Training on Dizziness, Vertigo Balance, Gait, and Quality of Life in Patients with Peripheral Vestibular Hypofunction: A Single-Blind, Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13026552.creator: Yasemin Apaydin, Çağla Özkul, Arzu Guclu-Gunduz, Umut Apaydin, Emre Orhan, Burak Kabiş, Ebru Şansal, Hakan Tutar, Bulent Gunduz
pmc-13026552.description: Background/Objectives: Peripheral vestibular hypofunction (PVH) commonly causes dizziness, imbalance, gait disturbances, and reduced quality of life. Task-oriented circuit training (TOCT) is a rehabilitation approach in which patients perform structured, task-specific functional movements repetitively to improve real-life motor performance. TOCT integrates functional, multisensory, and repetitive exercises based on motor learning and neuroplasticity principles, potentially enhancing rehabilitation outcomes.

pmc-13079527.title: Potential biomarkers and their recent applications ofr point-of-care biosensors for the diagnosis of malaria
pmc-13079527.creator: Leyla Karadurmus, Ahmet Cetinkaya, Pinar Kocabay, Menyar Ben Jaballah, Eva Baldrich, Sibel A. Ozkan
pmc-13079527.description: Malaria remains to be one of the deadliest infectious illnesses and is especially common in underdeveloped and developing countries. Recent advances (2022–2025) in biosensor engineering, nanomaterials, and microfluidic automation have significantly expanded the capabilities of point-of-care diagnostic technologies for malaria.

pmc-13087405.title: Inclusion bias affects common variant discovery and replication in a health-system linked biobank
pmc-13087405.creator: Aditya Pimplaskar, Junqiong Qiu, Sandra Lapinska, Veronica Tozzo, Jeffrey N. Chiang, Bogdan Pasaniuc, Loes M. Olde Loohuis
pmc-13087405.description: SummaryElectronic health record (EHR)-linked biobanks hold promise for precision medicine by enabling association studies between genetic variants and clinical phenotypes for individual risk assessment. However, most biobanks use opt-in consent protocols to recruit individuals interacting with healthcare systems. This strategy may lead to both participation and recruitment bias, the effects of which on genetic analyses remain understudied.

pmc-13296108.title: Digital health in palliative care: use is largely limited to conventional technologies – a cross-sectional survey of healthcare professionals
pmc-13296108.creator: Felix Muehlensiepen, Robert Darkow, Larissa Fink, Yuriy Ignatyev, Anne Gehlhaar, Anke Lauke, Marcel-Alexander Kamp, Martin Heinze, Matthew Allsop, Susann May

pmc-13326294.title: IL-17A deficiency in HLA-DR3 transgenic mice enriches beneficial Prevotella species in gut to promote Tregs and reduce CNS autoimmunity
pmc-13326294.creator: Shailesh K Shahi, Sudeep Ghimire, Samantha N Jensen, Peter C Lehman, Allison G Rux, Souradip Sinha, Nicholas Borcherding, Munir R Tanas, Katherine N Gibson-Corley, Sukirth M Ganesan, Nitin J Karandikar, Ashutosh K Mangalam
pmc-13326294.description: BackgroundHuman Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) class-II genes, particularly HLA-DR2 and HLA-DR3, and the gut microbiota are intricately linked to the pathobiology of multiple sclerosis (MS) through their ability to regulate host immunity, a critical factor in disease pathogenesis. An imbalance between anti-inflammatory CD4+ Tregs and pro-inflammatory IL-17A-secreting CD4+ Th17 cells is thought to drive disease.

pmc-13373850.title: Conserved symbiosis‐associated genes in the cycad Encephalartos natalensis suggest co‐option for cyanobacterial symbiosis
pmc-13373850.creator: Cassandra Schoeman, Danielle Roodt, Amy Mc Menamin, Oliver Bezuidt, Choaro Dithugoe, Desré Pinard, Eshchar Mizrachi
pmc-13373850.description: Summary Plant‐cyanobacterial symbioses have evolved independently at least four times across land plants, yet their underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here, we elucidate the pathways involved in this specialised symbiosis and nutrient exchange within coralloid roots (CRs) of Encephalartos natalensis.

pmc-13427537.title: Moving cardio-oncology upstream: Integrating cardiovascular prevention into routine cancer care
pmc-13427537.creator: Meiyan Liu
pmc-13427537.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). isk.1 Despite significant advances in the management of cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT), there remains a significant gap between basic research and clinical translation, and many healthcare centers worldwide still lack standardized cardio-oncology management pathways. This review integrates recent mechanistic insights with emerging clinical evidence to propose a practical framework for contemporary cardio-oncology care, and highlights critical unresolved challenges for future research.1 The four core pillars of modern cardio-oncology are illustrated in Figure 1 to clarify its core concepts and key priorities.

pmc-13437796.title: Bacteria-related signals in brain metastases: evidence boundaries, tumor-microenvironment remodeling, and translational prospects
pmc-13437796.creator: Guicheng Kuang, Zhenghaonan Qiu, Lingxiao Li, Jinjian Bai, Hang Ji, Yi Liu
pmc-13437796.description: Brain metastases (BrM) develop within a highly specialized central nervous system niche shaped by the blood–brain barrier/blood–tumor barrier, brain-resident stromal cells, myeloid populations, and distinct metabolic constraints. Emerging studies suggest that bacteria-related signals can be detected in primary and metastatic brain tumors; however, their biological meaning remains incompletely defined.
